mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least three consecutive months, lower real interest rates incentivize risk-taking by investors, leading to higher expected equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 60-day risk-free rate (t-test p > 0.05), or real GDP growth (GDPC1) does not accelerate meaningfully.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in labor market participation (HOUST) signals weakening labor demand, which typically precedes a sharp downward adjustment in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite a persistent downward trend in both PAYEMS and HOUST for at least 30 days post-trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two consecutive months predicts that the Federal Reserve will accelerate rate hikes, which reduces the present value of future cash flows and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are also negative over the next 5 days despite CPIAUCSL reverting to below 3% within 2 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust economic momentum that supports higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_12mo_avg for four consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite INDPRO remaining above its 12-month average for 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a sharp decline in unemployment (PAYEMS) but before wage growth accelerates (UNRATE), the persistence of low labor costs and weak wage pressures often coincides with a pause in rate hikes, which lowers real borrowing costs and tends to drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND UNRATE < previous month AND UNRATE growth < 0.1% over next 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns remain negative despite no change in FEDFUNDS over the same horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time spike in job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies) would typically coincide with rising labor demand proxies (e.g., HOUST), but in the absence of such proxies, a persistent decline in labor force participation (HOUST) for two consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as market anticipates softening demand.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous month AND HOUST < prior-to-previous month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive despite a downward trend in labor participation for 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not available; use GDPC1 as a broad demand proxy instead) is replaced here by a two-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) alongside a sharp drop in consumer confidence proxies (not available) — instead, we use a two-month drop in RSAFS (retail sales proxy) coupled with a one-month drop in HOUST (demand pressure), predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month AND INDPRO < prior-to-previous month AND HOUST < previous month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) even as the trigger proxies continue to decline.

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift from contractionary to accommodative monetary policy occurs when FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-year average for two consecutive months, which typically lowers financing costs and supports higher corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days in non-recessionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > FEDFUNDS_5yr_avg for two consecutive months AND not in recession regime (indicated by INDPRO > INDPRO_5yr_avg)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite FEDFUNDS remaining above its 5-year average for 90 days.
